about: Which Lean declaration formalises which ledger item, and how much of it. faithfulness: full = the declaration states the whole claim (literature inputs as explicit hypotheses or Published axioms), so a kernel proof promotes the item; core = a component of the claim is proved and the item keeps its status; statement = a typed statement whose proof is still owed (sorry). not_expressible names what Mathlib v4.33.1 lacks. inputs re-points literature items at their typed axioms.

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.conf_t.note: Conf_2(F) = ∅ iff F is injective; the automorphism step is Ax–Grothendieck
Conf_2(F) = ∅ iff F is an automorphism, with Ax–Grothendieck (injective → automorphism) and its converse as explicit hypotheses

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.confIm.note: the image of Conf_k is U_{≥k}, as sets; that q_k is étale and U_d is the proper locus are not formalised

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.conf_i.note: Conf_k = ∅ for k > d, given the fiber bound #F⁻¹(y) ≤ d as a hypothesis; the bound from the generic degree is the geometric input
the same over the geometric record, whose fiber bound is a field

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.card_c.note: over an m-point fiber Conf_k has (m)_k points; the Euler-characteristic identity is Euler integration of this count and is not formalised

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.card_e.note: the fiber of the forgetful map over an m-point fiber has m - (k-1) points; étaleness is not formalised

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.card_u.note: B_k over an m-point fiber has C(m,k) points
over a d-point fiber there is exactly one d-subset: B_d ≃ U_d as sets

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.partit.note: K_r(F) ≃ Σ_s Conf_{Fin r / s}(F) as sets, for every equivalence relation s on {1..r}; that the pieces are open and closed (KG-13) and the Stirling count of setoids with k classes are not formalised

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.config.note: the G-set of ordered k-tuples of distinct sheets is transitive iff G is k-transitive; identifying components of the cover with orbits is Riemann existence

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.card_t.note: the orderings of the d sheets have d!/|G| orbits under G ≤ S_d: the component count of the top configuration over the proper locus

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.card_e.note: a transitive action with trivial stabilisers has |G| = |X|; Campbell's criterion is the literature input

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.perfec.note: a perfect subgroup of S_d, d ≥ 2, is not S_d

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.nonmax.note: assuming the monodromy group is perfect (KG-PM01, the claim's own hypothesis), it is not the full symmetric group

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.sign_e.note: sign σ = (-1)^(b+q), Mathlib's form; b+q ≡ b-q mod 2

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.defici.note: in a perfect permutation group b+q is even

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.perfec.note: for an inertia permutation in a perfect monodromy group, b+q (equivalently b-q) is even

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.permSu.note: no permutation moves exactly one point

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.defici.note: supp σ + t = 1 forces supp σ = 0, t = 1

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.altern.note: no element of an alternating group has support of size two

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.degree.note: the deficit arithmetic from the external budget input

the deficit and support case analysis forcing the packet (3,1),(1,1),(1,1), from the external budget axiom and KG-PC01; it assumes KG-EM10 (exactly two components) and that the normalisation ramifies somewhere, so the claim is not verified by this

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.euler_.note: the arithmetic from the two Euler inputs

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.global.note: d - 1 = Σ_{m<d} (d-m) χ(U_m), with Euler integration over the source and additivity over the target as hypotheses

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.fiberD.note: d - m_C = |supp σ_C| + t_C, by counting the d sheets over a generic point of C; m_C and t_C are read off the record's sheetInSource and the coherence field sheetInSource_disjoint_support (the Keller map is étale on its source, so a sheet the inertia moves is not in it); no other hypothesis

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.etaleM.note: an étale-maximal map has no (d-1)-point fiber

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.topCon.note: the contrapositive of KG-PC03, derived from it

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.generi.note: a generically unramified boundary divisor is everywhere étale, is A¹, and maps as the normalisation

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.delete.note: a deleted sheet lies over a multibranch component

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.allCom.note: the derivation of the unibranch criterion from KG-EM03, which is assumed as the hypothesis hmb and is itself still an open hole; the claim is not verified by this

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.incide.note: a component is adjacent to a point it has a branch over

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.reacha.note: components linked through the points are linked in the incidence graph

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.exists.note: a listed point lying on the curve lies on some component

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.incide.note: a connected curve has a connected incidence graph

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.exists.note: every incidence edge is a component–point pair with a branch

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.card_e.note: the incidence edges inject into the pairs with a branch

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.card_p.note: with a double branch somewhere, the pairs with a branch number at most Σb − 1

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.card_a.note: a connected curve with a self-identification has c + |points| ≤ Σ_p r_p

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.euler_.note: the Euler bound χ = c − Σ_p (r_p − 1) ≤ 0 for a connected curve with a self-identification

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.connec.note: the derivation of EM-7 from Jelonek's Euler positivity: connectedness plus a self-identification forces χ(S_F) ≤ 0. It assumes the Euler count off the A¹ normalisations and the multibranch consequence of non-maximality (KG-EM02 with KG-EM03), both unproved here, so the claim is not verified by this

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.nonmax.note: the contrapositive, derived, carrying the same two assumed prerequisites

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.disjoi.note: components in different connected components of S_F are disjoint, meeting generating the connected components

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.exists.note: a disconnected S_F has two components in different connected components

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.discon.note: a disconnected S_F lies in one rational one-place pencil with every connected component irreducible; from Jelonek's parametrisation and Assi's trichotomy as Published axioms, with connected components defined as the classes generated by meeting and the record's coherence field disjoint_of_pencilOf_eq (distinct members of one pencil are disjoint); verified once those two inputs are admitted

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.two_le.note: a disconnected S_F selects at least two fibers

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.common.note: exactly two selected fibers and a noncoordinate pencil, in the disconnected common-pencil case of a counterexample; from Assi's dichotomy and Braun–Dias–Venato-Santos as Published axioms, with the count of selected fibers defined as the number of components; verified once those two inputs are admitted

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.nonmax.note: the two-nodal-fiber derivation from KG-EM07, KG-EM08, KG-EM09 and Assi's equinodal theorem, free of any Lean hole; it carries KG-EM07's two assumed prerequisites, so the claim is not verified by this

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.onePla.note: each component has normalisation A¹ and one place at infinity, from Jelonek's parametrisation and Chau's theorem as Published axioms; verified once those two inputs are admitted

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.nonmax.note: the group-theoretic step of PM-1: perfectness follows once the nodal vanishing cycles are assumed to generate the sheet monodromy with each generator a ratio of conjugate branch inertias. Those are the audit's own two load-bearing points and both are assumed here, so the claim is not verified by this

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.degree.note: A₆ from the external six-sheet frontier (an ExternalResearch axiom) and perfectness; verified once that input is admitted

the disjointness of the two branch inertias at a node, derived from the packet; it assumes that the branch meridians are conjugate to the generic meridian and that their supports exhaust the sheets (the zero-excess census KG-A602), so the claim is not verified by this

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.conjug.note: a ratio of conjugate elements is a commutator

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.perfec.note: a group generated by ratios of conjugate elements is perfect

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.permSu.note: trivial support means the trivial permutation
conjugate permutations move the same number of letters

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.disjoi.note: two permutations whose supports cover every letter, with sizes summing to at most the number of letters, have disjoint supports
